content.title: About
content.content: Sesame oil is extracted from the seeds of the sesame plant (Sesamum indicum). It is widely used in Asian cuisine as well as in cosmetics and aromatherapy. The oil has a characteristic nutty aroma, light‑yellow color, and a relatively high smoke point.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sesame is one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for more than 5,000 years.
In Japan and China, sesame oil is traditionally served cold over rice and sushi.
Sesame seeds contain over 50 % oil, making them one of the most oil‑rich seeds.
Toasted (dark) sesame oil has a stronger, richer flavor than untoasted (light) oil.
Sesame oil is commonly used in Ayurvedic massage for its warming properties.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Contains vitamin E and sesamol, which protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Beneficial fatty acids
items.content: High in polyunsaturated fats, especially omega‑6 linoleic acid, supporting skin and heart health.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Sesame seeds are a good source of calcium and magnesium, which benefit bone density.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory properties
items.content: Sesamol and sesamin may help reduce inflammation in the body.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: The oil stimulates bile production, improving fat digestion.

items.title: Sesame allergy
items.content: Sesame is a potent allergen; sensitive individuals can experience severe reactions.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Like all plant oils, sesame oil is calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Omega‑6 balance
items.content: Excessive omega‑6 intake without enough omega‑3 may promote inflammation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use sesame oil for stir‑frying, salad dressings, marinades, and sauces. Dark toasted oil is added to finished dishes for flavor, while light oil works well in baking and desserts. One to two teaspoons per day provide the benefits.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the oil in a tightly sealed bottle in a cool, dark place. After opening, keep it refrigerated to slow oxidation. Discard if it develops a rancid smell.
